name: Tom Ford
origin: Founded in 2006 by Tom Ford after leaving Gucci.
opview: “Dressing well is a form of good manners.”

notes.status: Status through a very specific idea of the glamorous man, held without irony since the Gucci years. The tailoring is the tell, and it is meant to be.
notes.ivy: fluent rather than native — the collegiate canon spoken in a Hollywood accent, by a house founded in 2005 on glamour
notes.prep: held at 4 on the reading of a prep authority who calls it the best contemporary take on the register; the founding wardrobes keep the 5

notes.style: Sharp, glamorous tailoring to one designer's exact taste.
notes.craft: Tom Ford PDPs state a country of make (Italy, Portugal) and composition, with no factory, mill or tannery named. Zegna Group's page says the group runs Tom Ford Fashion end-to-end 'through to production', but on the pages I read it does not say that Zegna-owned plants make Tom Ford products. The current 2 holds unless the group's Filiera page or report confirms owned making for specific categories.

cities: 10 stores, including Las Vegas, Atlanta, Beverly Hills · department stores and independent menswear shops, and its own site

craft_evidence.owned_d: The brand site claims no owned factory. Parent: Zegna Group's Tom Ford Fashion brand page says the group 'currently oversees end-to-end the TOM FORD FASHION business...from collection creation and development to merchandising, through to production'. That is oversight of production, not a statement that Zegna-owned plants make Tom Ford products. I did not reach the Zegna 'Our Filiera' page (zegnagroup.com/en/our-filiera/) or the annual/sustainability report, which might say whether group-owned plants make TF (tailoring, knitwear or leather). Unverified.
craft_evidence.countries: Italy 2/4 (suede bomber, cashmere sweater), Portugal 1/4 (piquet polo), not visible 1/4 (mohair-wool suit, where origin may sit in a details tab the fetch could not see) (sample of 4 PDPs).
